newsitem.title: CHINA: Intel to move half flash memory output to China.
newsitem.headline: Intel to move half flash memory output to China.

text.p: Intel Corp wants to see half of its global assembly capacity for flash memory chips moved to a new plant in Shanghai, a senior company official said on Wednesday.

Intel's executive vice-president Gerry Parker said in an interview that the company had decided to invest $99 million in a plant in one of Shanghai's free trade zones to assemble and test flash memory chips. Production is due to begin in mid-1998.
Almost all of Intel's flash memory assembly capacity, with a end-value of around $800 million a year, is currently concentrated in one factory in Manila.
"I would like ultimately to produce half our flash output in this factory, half here and half in Manila," Parker said.

"We'll shift a little production from Manila, and pull some of our sub-contractors (in Japan) down. But the flash business is growing pretty rapidly, so by the time this factory is up and running we'll have doubled our output anyway," he said.

Parker said the factory had not been set up to feed the domestic China market, which is still very small by global standards. "It's an emerging market, we want to be here and have a presence here," he said.
